item.title: Provisional Seestar S30 Pro / S50 Pro T CrB Photometry Guide
item.description:
Provisional, early days. Photometry with a Seestar is new: the app's Photometry mode only arrived in v3.4.0 (October 2026), and ZWO has not yet published how it works. This is a short guide to getting good frames, written from early tests with an S30 Pro. I will keep updating it as I get better information and more data, so expect the advice to change. Treat it as a starting point and check it yourself.
First version: 19 October 2026. See the update log at the bottom.

What you need

  • A Seestar S30 Pro or S50 Pro with a recent app. These steps come from an S30 Pro; the S50 Pro should be similar, but check each point on your own frames.
  • AAVSO’s comparison stars for T CrB, free from the AAVSO Variable Star Plotter.

1. Choose your stars

Open the AAVSO Variable Star Plotter, enter T CrB (chart X43296GGQ) and note the comparison stars close to T CrB’s brightness, about magnitude 10 to 11. Stars 102, 106, 107 and 112 (V 10.17 to 11.17) work well. Avoid much brighter stars: they are too bright for the camera and give bad readings.

item.title: Seestar Variable Star Observing Manual
item.description: Status: first draft, building this out as we go. Every claim here is attributed to a real source — AAVSO’s own documentation, or a named person in a public forum post, with the date. Where we add our own measurements and steps (S30 Pro, T CrB, October 2026), they are labelled as ours, are provisional, and are covered in more detail in the provisional T CrB photometry guide. Where sources disagree, both sides are here rather than picked for you. Nothing below is invented; if a step isn’t sourced yet, it isn’t in here yet.
